output_text: In the old hospital’s unused X-ray room, rented by the museum as overflow storage, Elias the forger propped his varnish-tacky Madonna against a radiator and raised the small round shaving mirror on its tarnished brass stand, the silvering flaked away along one curved edge. In its spotted glass the blue mantle reversed into a brittle fan of strokes—too even at the hem, too cautious around the fingers—and, when the therapist from next door came looking for her missing mirror, he lowered the failed copy and handed it back by the stem. When told to touch thumb to finger, she moved only the right, then stared at the drooping hand in the brass-framed reflection as the therapist pressed a warm towel into its palm and said, “That one too; it’s yours.”
